primary_claim: DPO and RLHF trained AIs put nonzero weight on spurious features even in the infinite-data limit, and a proposed mitigation, 'tie training' (training on pairs of equal true value with balanced/random labels), markedly reduces spurious weights and improves out-of-distribution generalization, e.g. raising adversarial accuracy on a hotel-choice task from 64% (strict preferences) to 87% (30% informative ties) in Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct.

effect.value: 64% (strict-preference training) vs 87% (30% informative ties) vs 77% (30% non-informative ties); in-distribution accuracy essentially unchanged (92% vs 91-92%)

stated_future_work: Use bigger models and real-world data
Test whether tie training can mitigate real-world misalignments like verbosity bias, sycophancy, and apparent-success-seeking
Try to prove similar theoretical results for RLVR
Devise and test versions of tie training designed for RLVR
limitations_stated: LLM experiments use Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct and synthetic (hotel-recommendation) data
The linear utility function assumption underlying the theorems is not literally true for neural networks and LLMs
quote: Tie training improves adversarial performance substantially, at essentially no in-distribution cost.
